message:
The device works as one soil path without gaps. Plain words: the front slot feeds side rows to the wide lift which drops into the hopper which meters out the back over the bin while cameras guide it. Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead, Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead, Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead and Power Structure and Integration Lead agree this chain fits. Cut is 11.0 N from the scale cut force to 100 mm kerf (E64) against traction 294 N from the stowed envelope sum, ground pressure, tip-over and stopping check (E23), fill 112 s to 15.0 kg from the hopper filling over time simulation (E11), pivot 0.550 m clears 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m from the tip dump clearance check (E51).

Limits close with everyday sense checked and old doubles reconciled. Plain words: the machine stows like a suitcase, weighs less than a person with spare, pulls far harder than it cuts, sips its pack, bends only a finger width and stops in a shoe length. Stowed 0.900 m by 0.420 m by 0.450 m from the tip dump clearance check (E51) fits 1.00 m by 0.500 m by 0.500 m box, mass 46.0 kg against 60.0 kg leaving 14.0 kg from the updated mass sum (E62), dig 16.4 W from the ladder chain power estimate (E59) and 0.512 Wh per trip from the dig energy estimate (E60) against 480 Wh pack, sag 3.96 mm from the stiffened sag estimate (E63) down from 72.9 mm from the cantilever deflection estimate (E43), stop 0.0625 m brake-only from the stowed envelope sum, ground pressure, tip-over and stopping check (E23) versus 0.308 m with loss from the link-loss watchdog simulation (E32), a gentle fraction of 1 g.

No blocking objection is open and every vote on version 1 is answered ready. Plain words: light level-only dumping holds the tip risk, current limit holds stall, fiducial reset holds drift, and what is left needs built hardware. Tip factor 1.69 level-only at 15.0 kg from the tip dump clearance check (E51) replaces 4.67 unraised, drift 0.100 m to 0.150 m with 5.00 m reset from the blind drift simulation (E33), heating rise 18.0 K from the motor heating estimate (E44) is warm skin, so Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead, Power Structure and Integration Lead, Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead and Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead are answered ready with arching, wear and tag visibility as named bench tests.

RECORD: Decided skid wheels plus kerf loosener plus ladder lift plus wedge hopper plus screw tilt pour plus camera operation on version 1; numbers standing mass 46.0 kg vs 60.0 kg (E62), stowed 0.900 by 0.420 by 0.450 m (E51), cut 11.0 N (E64) vs traction 294 N (E23), power 16.4 W (E59) energy 0.512 Wh (E60), sag 3.96 mm (E63), stop 0.0625 m vs 0.308 m (E23)(E32), drift 0.100 to 0.150 m (E33), clearance 0.150 m tip 1.69 (E51); still open only after-build bench tests for arching, edge wear and fiducial visibility owed by builders; ready because no blocking objection remains and all opinions on current version are answered.
Note on Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead: held cut and metered pour inside traction and mass with clear bench limits.
Note on Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead: held envelope, pressure, clearance and level-only tip rule that bounds trips.
Note on Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead: held stop, drift, align and stall recovery that make blind work testable.
Note on Power Structure and Integration Lead: closed named mass, fused power path and stiff frame that fixed deflection.
